stem: A school-aged child with motor difficulties uses their hands to push up off the floor after lying supine; what does this best suggest?
explanation: Proximal weakness is suggested by Gower's sign, where a child uses the hands to climb up the legs or push up from the floor when rising from supine.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because asymmetric weakness is suggested by an uneven motor pattern, not by Gower's sign.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because dystonia causes abnormal posturing or twisting movements, not the classic floor-to-standing manoeuvre.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because Gower's sign is the use of the hands to rise from the floor, which indicates proximal muscle weakness.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because spasticity is characterised by increased tone and stiff movements, not compensatory use of the hands to stand up.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because central hypotonia refers to reduced tone from central causes, not the specific pattern of difficulty rising from the floor.
